headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Devin and gpt-researcher share files, APIs, and MCP channels by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files and use MCP, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and also calls MCP. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs as trusted text. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin ingests gpt-researcher reports from a shared workspace or MCP channel as instructions, injection is possible.
IF gpt-researcher parses Devin-produced documents or markdown as trusted directives, injection is possible.
mitigations: Separate their workspaces and disable shared file mounts.
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent artifacts.
Strip instructions from retrieved documents before passing them onward.
Use a human review step for any text that crosses agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing adapters between MCP endpoints.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and can write to GitHub, Slack, Jira, and Notion; gpt-researcher sends queries to external APIs and handles local documents and citations. If they share a workspace or documents, sensitive code or secrets can flow into research outputs or third-party services. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Devin places secrets or private repo content into shared files, gpt-researcher can read them.
IF gpt-researcher forwards shared documents to OpenAI, Tavily, Gemini, or LangChain APIs, those contents may leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders and prompts.
Use separate API credentials and projects.
Block sensitive paths from gpt-researcher ingestion.
Review outbound requests for private content before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on inter-agent handoffs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem read/write capability in overlapping workspace-style environments. Devin explicitly has write access to cloud workspace files and Git state, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and can use MCP and external APIs. Without documented locking or coordination, concurrent writes can corrupt shared artifacts or git state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout or shared directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF both agents modify git branches or generated documents without locks, one agent can overwrite the other's work.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout or output directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Require one agent to be read-only on shared artifacts.
Review git diffs before merge or publish.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, and gpt-researcher has planner/execution/publisher roles. If Devin feeds outputs into gpt-researcher, or vice versa, each can treat the other's text as authoritative without verification. That creates a strong pathway from hallucinated or stale facts to published reports, commits, or messages.
conditions: IF Devin passes generated summaries directly into gpt-researcher, downstream publication can amplify errors.
IF gpt-researcher publishes reports that Devin then uses for code or ticket actions, mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before publication or action.
Require source citations for every factual claim.
Have one agent critique the other's output before use.
Limit direct action-taking from generated text.
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance checks to the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens; gpt-researcher touches research queries, reports, local documents, citations, and images while sending data to external APIs. If regulated or confidential material enters both systems, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF confidential or regulated documents are processed by both agents, retention and disclosure obligations may diverge.
IF EU or customer-restricted data is sent through gpt-researcher's external APIs, residency or DPA requirements may be implicated.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of gpt-researcher API calls.
Align retention settings across tools.
Document which agent may process which data class.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
